title: Area and Perimeter Formulas
short: Use A = l × w and P = 2l + 2w, and work backward to a missing side.
trouble: Children add the length and width once for perimeter, forgetting the other two sides.

blocks.html: In Grade 3 you found area and perimeter by counting squares and adding sides. With two-digit multiplication you can use formulas for rectangles of any size.

For a rectangle with length $l$ and width $w$: area $A = l \times w$ (square units) and perimeter $P = 2 \times l + 2 \times w$ (units). To find a missing side, work backward: $w = A \div l$, or take $2 \times l$ away from the perimeter and halve what is left.

Area counts unit squares: $w$ rows of $l$ squares is $l \times w$. Perimeter walks around the outside: along a length, a width, the other length and the other width. Opposite sides of a rectangle are equal, so that is two lengths and two widths.

blocks.title: Area and perimeter
blocks.q: A garden is 12 feet long and 7 feet wide. Find its area and perimeter.

blocks.title: A missing side from the perimeter
blocks.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 30 cm and a length of 9 cm. How wide is it?
steps: The two widths share the rest: $30 - 18 = 12$ cm.

blocks.title: A missing side from the area
blocks.q: A rug has an area of 96 square feet and a length of 12 feet. How wide is it?

blocks.html: Adding the length and width only once for the perimeter ($12 + 7 = 19$ feet). That is only half the trip around. Trace all four sides with your finger, or use $2 \times l + 2 \times w$.
